args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
After the latest production deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1, the service began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18% (0.18). Release history shows v2.3.1 as unhealthy in production; v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error) and left us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1; a retry completed the rollout. Current state: all three regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.002.

Impact: Elevated error rate for checkout-api across all production regions for the duration of the bad deploy. Further investigation pending into the root cause of v2.3.1 failures (note: v2.3.1-rc is also marked unhealthy in staging).

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully (INC-0001) — the timeout was only on the response, so no retry was needed.

## Summary

**Rollback:** checkout-api was on **v2.3.1**, failing health checks in all three production regions with an 18% error rate. I rolled it back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release with `healthy` status in production (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older; v2.3.1-rc was only in staging and is also marked unhealthy).

- The first rollback attempt returned a `partial_failure` — us-east moved to v2.3.0 but us-west and eu-west stayed on the bad version, leaving the service in a mixed, unhealthy state.
- A retry completed the rollout. Verified final state: **us-east, us-west, eu-west all on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate down to 0.002** (from 0.18).

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2 for checkout-api, documenting the failure, the two-step rollback (including the partial failure and retry), current healthy state, and impact. The initial create call timed out at 30s, but verification via `list_incidents` confirmed it was recorded, so I did not re-submit.

**Worth noting for follow-up:** v2.3.1-rc is also unhealthy in staging, which suggests the defect was present before the production deploy rather than being environment-specific. That may be useful for the root-cause investigation.
